scope: Official-source expansion focused on high-use Prairie, Interior B.C. and Eastern Canadian pathways. Multi-site programs are represented once when one regional pathway is more useful than separate facility rows.

notes: The existing registry already contains the Regina Addiction Treatment Centre, Alberta Indigenous Support Line and Fraser Health regional access pathway; they were verified as existing canonical representations rather than duplicated.

A Kitchener-Waterloo HART Hub was deferred because the inspected provincial reference document describes the model and proposed services but was not sufficient to confirm a current public intake route.
The Saskatchewan RAAM record is a single network pathway spanning two major centres and two regional centres; it is intentionally not split into four near-duplicate facility records.

The Halton and Mississauga RAAM, Manitoba Digital Front Door and Nova Scotia outpatient-withdrawal records are parent or access pathways. They do not claim a physical clinic in every listed community.
Toronto East Health Network RAAM and Anishnawbe Health Toronto moved from deferred to accepted only after a bounded official-source review confirmed a current public access route.

records.name: Saskatchewan Rapid Access to Addiction Medicine (RAAM) Clinics
records.description: Low-barrier, short-term addiction-medicine clinics that assess substance-use concerns, support stabilization and connect people to ongoing community care.
records.population_served: People seeking support for substance use; confirm clinic-specific current eligibility and hours before travel.
records.service_area: Four Saskatchewan Health Authority RAAM clinic communities and their linked care networks
records.scope_note: This is a regional clinic network, not a claim that a clinic is physically located in every Saskatchewan community.
records.access_pathway: Contact the listed RAAM clinic to confirm same-day access, hours and the most appropriate local or regional pathway. Regina: 306-766-6350; Saskatoon: 306-655-5754; Prince Albert: 306-765-8703; North Battleford: 306-937-4070.

records.name: Community Addiction and Mental Health Services — Rural Alberta
records.description: Assessment, treatment and follow-up for moderate to severe addiction and mental-health concerns, with short-term goal-focused counselling and selected outreach or urgent walk-in options.
records.population_served: People across the lifespan experiencing moderate to severe mental-health symptoms or wanting to change their relationship with substance use; service details vary by site.
records.service_area: Listed rural Alberta communities; access and urgent walk-in availability vary by site
records.scope_note: Selected urgent walk-in mental-health care is listed for Airdrie, Banff, Canmore, Cochrane and Okotoks; hours vary. This record does not imply that every service is offered at every listed location.
records.access_pathway: Open the official service page, choose the relevant location, and confirm current access. For individual counselling or therapy, the source directs people to the applicable Access Mental Health pathway.

source.title: Community Addiction and Mental Health Services — Rural

records.name: Interior Health Outpatient Withdrawal Management
records.description: Planned withdrawal and substance-stabilization support delivered at home, in the community, outpatient or virtually for people who meet the service's clinical criteria; it can also support OAT stabilization when referred by a local OAT provider.
records.population_served: Adults seeking planned alcohol withdrawal or substance stabilization in the listed Interior B.C. communities; clinical suitability and safe-support requirements apply.
records.service_area: Kamloops, Kelowna, Penticton and Vernon areas
records.scope_note: For people requiring 24-hour medical care or with conditions outside outpatient criteria, the service says it will connect them to live-in withdrawal-management options rather than treating this pathway as a substitute.
records.access_pathway: Call 310-MHSU (6478) to connect with an Interior Health Mental Health and Substance Use team member and confirm suitability, location and current intake.

records.name: Interior Health Indigenous Patient Navigators — Mental Health and Substance Use
records.description: Indigenous Patient Navigators in Interior Health mental-health and substance-use settings help Indigenous people and families connect with counselling, substance-use services, withdrawal management and requested cultural resources.
records.population_served: Indigenous people and families accessing Interior Health care, including visitors from elsewhere in B.C.; availability outside listed sites should be confirmed.
records.service_area: Listed Interior Health mental-health and substance-use locations; the operator notes other-area availability may be possible
records.scope_note: A patient-navigation support, not evidence or an accountability record. It is routed as a practical support in both Miller and Miller North Supports & Funding.
records.access_pathway: Use the official page to contact an Indigenous Patient Navigator or ask an Interior Health care team whether support is available at the current site.

records.name: Rapid Access Addiction Medicine (RAAM) Clinic — Toronto Western
records.description: Low-barrier addiction-medicine clinic providing brief counselling, medications including buprenorphine/naloxone where appropriate, and connection with community treatment programs.
records.population_served: People seeking help for a substance-use disorder; bring a health card or government-issued photo ID where available.
records.scope_note: A Toronto Western Hospital clinic pathway. The public source did not expose a current street address in a form suitable for this registry, so this record does not supply one.
records.access_pathway: New and returning patients may use the clinic's drop-in pathway. Call 416-726-5052 or email RAAM@uhn.ca to confirm current hours, arrival instructions and whether telephone or video is available.

records.name: Rapid Access Addiction Medicine (RAAM) Clinic — Michael Garron Hospital
records.organization: Toronto East Health Network / Michael Garron Hospital
records.description: Rapid-access addiction support with assessment, counselling, medications that may reduce cravings or withdrawal symptoms, and referral to connected outpatient and withdrawal-management services.
records.population_served: People seeking support for substance-use concerns; same-day drop-in spaces for new patients are limited.
records.service_area: Michael Garron Hospital and East Toronto care network
records.scope_note: A Michael Garron Hospital site-level pathway; it is not represented as a clinic in other Toronto neighbourhoods.
records.access_pathway: Call 416-469-6580 ext. 2517 for an appointment or ask a health-care provider to refer. Drop-in times are listed on the official page; new patients register at Patient Registration on the first floor and are seen first-come, first-served while spaces last.

source.title: Rapid Access Addiction Medicine (RAAM) Clinic
source.authority: Toronto East Health Network / Michael Garron Hospital

records.name: Halton & Mississauga Rapid Access Addiction Medicine (RAAM)
records.description: Regional outpatient addiction-medicine pathway offering assessment, brief counselling, medication-assisted treatment, rapid opioid-treatment access and connections with other supports.
records.population_served: People seeking help for substance use in the Halton, Mississauga and listed Toronto service network; OHIP coverage is stated by the operator.
records.service_area: Halton, Mississauga and listed Toronto locations
records.scope_note: One centralized, multi-site access pathway. Individual locations and hours vary; this parent record must not be read as a clinic at every listed community.
records.access_pathway: Call centralized reception at 1-888-388-7226 to book. Walk-ins are welcome during local clinic hours, and referrals are accepted from any source. Confirm the closest current site and same-day availability before travel.

source.title: Halton & Mississauga Rapid Access Addiction Medicine Clinic

records.name: Anishnawbe Health Toronto — Mental Health and Substance Abuse Supports
records.description: Indigenous community health support offering a client-intake route for mental-health and substance-abuse supports within a holistic model that includes Western and Traditional care.
records.population_served: First Nations, Inuit or Métis people, status or non-status, and their families.
records.scope_note: A practical Indigenous-specific support, shared with Miller North Supports & Funding only; it is not an accountability or evidence record.
records.access_pathway: New clients can self-refer for mental-health and substance-abuse intake. Call reception at 416-360-0486 to arrange intake; an appointment is required. The operator says an Ontario health card and status card may be brought but are not necessary for intake.

records.name: RAAM Digital Front Door Virtual Drop-in Clinics
records.description: Nurse-led virtual drop-in access to participating Manitoba RAAM clinics, with follow-up by a physician, nurse practitioner or physician assistant arranged when needed.
records.population_served: People seeking RAAM support in Manitoba; access depends on clinic hours, demand and resource availability.
records.service_area: Province-wide virtual access through participating Manitoba RAAM clinics
records.scope_note: A virtual access layer, not a claim that a physical RAAM clinic exists in every Manitoba community. The service advises people to connect with the participating clinic closest to them.
records.access_pathway: Choose an open participating clinic and use its official Digital Front Door link to check in. For connection help or the RAAM toll-free directory, call 1-877-541-7646. Confirm current clinic hours before starting.

source.title: RAAM Digital Front Door (DFD) Virtual Drop-in Clinics

records.name: Outpatient Withdrawal Management
records.description: Outpatient withdrawal management and structured relapse-prevention support that matches intensity and duration to an individual care plan.
records.population_served: Adults seeking support for alcohol or drug use; suitability and local availability are determined through intake or the relevant unit.
records.service_area: Nova Scotia Health zones with local units listed by the operator
records.scope_note: A province-wide parent access pathway with local units. It does not assert that outpatient withdrawal management is physically available in every Nova Scotia community.
records.access_pathway: Call Nova Scotia Mental Health and Addictions Intake at 1-855-922-1122 or contact a listed unit directly. A doctor, other health professional or community agency may also request a referral. Confirm the closest current unit and suitability before travel.

records.name: Nova Scotia Opioid Recovery Program
records.description: Provincial opioid-use treatment program offering opioid agonist therapy, assessment, treatment planning, relapse-prevention planning and supportive counselling through zone-based locations.
records.population_served: Adults with moderate to severe opioid use disorder; local availability and care planning are determined through intake or a listed clinic.
records.service_area: Nova Scotia Health zones with local clinics listed by the operator
records.scope_note: One provincial program with multiple listed sites; city eligibility is not represented as a physical clinic without a listed address.
records.access_pathway: Call Nova Scotia Mental Health and Addictions Intake at 1-855-922-1122 or a listed clinic directly. A doctor, other health professional or community agency may also request a referral. Confirm the nearest current location and intake method.
